Standard recessed downlight in the center of the room
Linear LED wall-grazer placed very close to the wall
questions.n: Placing the light source at an acute angle to the surface emphasizes the shadows and highlights of the texture.

questions.q: According to the PEC, what is the maximum number of 15-amp receptacles allowed on a single residential branch circuit?
questions.n: Unlike some codes, the PEC generally requires sizing circuits based on the expected VA load, though a rule of thumb for general-purpose circuits is often 8-12.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of 'De-rating' a wire's ampacity?
o: To compensate for the weight of the conduit
To save money on copper by using smaller wires
To account for heat buildup when many wires are in one conduit
To allow for a lower voltage utility connection
questions.n: When current flows, it generates heat; if too many wires are grouped together, they cannot cool effectively, so their capacity must be reduced.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common symptom of 'Harmonics' in a building's electrical system, often caused by massive amounts of computers and LED lighting?
o: Reduction in the monthly water bill
questions.n: Harmonic currents (specifically the 3rd harmonic) do not cancel out in the neutral wire and can cause it to carry more current than the hot wires.

questions.q: What is the standard name for the diagram that shows the entire electrical system from the service entrance down to the smallest branch circuit in a single schematic?
questions.n: A one-line (or single-line) diagram simplifies the 3-phase system into a single line to show the overall logic and components of the power distribution.

questions.q: In the Philippines, which government agency provides the 'Occupancy Permit,' which usually requires the CEI (Certificate of Electrical Inspection) to be completed first?
questions.n: The OBO is the local government authority that ensures the building is safe and complies with all codes before it can be used.

questions.q: Which lighting term refers to the ability of a light source to show the 'true' colors of an object compared to natural sunlight?
questions.n: A higher CRI (closer to 100) means colors will look more natural and vibrant under that light source.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a 'Ballast' in an older fluorescent lighting fixture?
o: To change the color of the light
To provide the high starting voltage and then limit the current
To turn the light off when no one is in the room
To act as a backup battery
questions.n: Fluorescent lamps need a 'kick' to start and then a 'governor' to prevent the lamp from drawing too much power and destroying itself.

questions.q: When calculating the load for a building, the PEC allows 'Non-coincident Loads' (like Heating and Cooling) to be handled in what way?
o: You use an average of the two
You only count the larger of the two loads
You must add them both together
You must ignore both of them
questions.n: Since you will never run the air conditioning and the heaters at the same time, you only need to size the system for the one that draws more power.

questions.q: What is the standard 'clearance' required in front of an electrical panel board according to the PEC to allow an electrician to work safely?
questions.n: This 'working space' must be kept clear at all times to ensure that someone can quickly reach the breakers in an emergency.

questions.q: Which of the following describes 'Inductive' loads, which often cause a lower power factor in industrial buildings?
questions.n: Devices with coils of wire (like motors) create electromagnetic fields that cause the current to 'lag' behind the voltage.

questions.q: In the context of the PEC, what does the term 'Ampacity' specifically refer to?
o: The total amount of voltage in a circuit
The maximum current a wire can carry continuously without exceeding its temperature rating
questions.n: Ampacity is the 'safe limit' for a wire; exceeding it causes the insulation to melt and wires to catch fire.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the 'Bus Bar' in an electrical panel board?
o: To provide a place for the electrician to sit
To act as a central 'spine' to distribute power to multiple circuit breakers
To measure the electricity used by the neighbors
To hold the panel door closed
questions.n: Instead of using many small wires, a heavy metal bar allows for a clean, high-capacity way to connect all the breakers to the main power.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'Passive' fire protection measure often required where electrical conduits pass through a fire-rated wall?
questions.n: Firestopping seals the gaps around conduits to prevent smoke and flames from moving between rooms during a fire.

questions.q: What happens to the 'Voltage Drop' in a circuit as the distance from the power source increases?
o: The voltage drop stays the same
questions.n: More wire means more resistance, which 'steals' more voltage before it reaches the appliance at the end of the line.

questions.q: In a generator's fuel system, what is the 'Day Tank'?
o: A tank used only during the daytime
A smaller tank located near the generator that holds enough fuel for several hours of operation
A tank used to store rainwater for cooling
The main storage tank buried underground
questions.n: The day tank is fed from a larger bulk tank; it ensures the generator has immediate access to fuel without relying on long, external pump lines.

questions.q: What is the primary technical reason for using 3-phase power for large central air conditioning compressors in commercial buildings?
o: 3-phase motors are smaller and more efficient for the same horsepower
3-phase power is cheaper to buy from the utility
It prevents the lights from flickering when the AC turns on
The code bans single-phase power in all commercial buildings
questions.n: Because the power delivery is constant (the phases overlap), motors run more smoothly and require less copper to achieve the same work.

questions.q: Which lighting fixture is designed to distribute light in a 360-degree horizontal pattern, often used for illuminating walkways from a low height?
questions.n: Bollards are short, sturdy posts that house a light source, providing safety lighting for pedestrians without creating glare at eye level.

questions.q: In a residential panel board, why is the 'Neutral' bar bonded to the 'Ground' bar?
o: To save the electrician from having to install two separate bars
Because the PEC forbids having two different bars in the same box
To double the amount of voltage available
To ensure that a fault current has a low-resistance path back to the source to trip the breaker
questions.n: Bonding at the main service ensures that if a 'hot' wire touches a metal casing, the electricity flows back to the panel and immediately trips the breaker.

questions.q: What is the standard 'height' for a residential wall receptacle from the finished floor to the center of the box, according to common Philippine practice (though it can vary by design)?
questions.n: 12 inches (or 30cm) is the standard mounting height that keeps outlets accessible but low enough to be unobtrusive.

questions.q: Which component in an electrical system is designed to 'step up' or 'step down' voltage using the principle of mutual induction?
questions.n: Transformers use magnetic fields to transfer energy between two coils of wire, allowing voltage to be changed with very little energy loss.

questions.q: What is a 'Dedicated Circuit'?
o: A circuit that uses only gold-plated wires
A circuit that only works during the day
A branch circuit that serves only one specific piece of equipment
A circuit that cannot be turned off
questions.n: High-draw appliances like ACUs, ranges, and pumps get their own circuit so they don't trip a breaker when other things turn on.

questions.q: In lighting, what does the term 'Glare' refer to?
o: The color of the light bulb
Excessive brightness that causes visual discomfort or reduces visibility
A type of modern LED fixture
The amount of energy saved by a fixture
questions.n: Glare happens when there is a high contrast between a light source and its surroundings, or when light reflects directly into the eyes.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most energy-efficient light source available for architectural use today?
questions.n: LEDs produce the most light (lumens) per watt of energy used and last significantly longer than other technologies.

questions.q: What is the function of the 'Ground Fault' protection on a main circuit breaker in a commercial building?
o: To make the electricity 'cleaner' for computers
To detect if the neighbors are stealing power
To protect people from minor electric shocks in the bathroom
To prevent fires by detecting low-level faults that don't trip a standard breaker
questions.n: Large systems can have 'arcing' faults that are dangerous but don't draw enough current to trip a 1000-amp breaker instantly.

questions.q: In the Philippines, what is the standard 'Phase' for a typical residential service entrance?
questions.n: Most homes only need 230V single-phase power for lights, appliances, and small AC units.

questions.q: What is the primary architectural purpose of a 'Lighting Control System' (like Lutron or KNX) in a luxury hotel?
o: To replace the building's main generator
To make the lights brighter than normal bulbs allow
To create and recall 'Scenes' for different times of day
To eliminate the need for a lighting designer
questions.n: Architects use control systems to change the mood of a lobby or restaurant with one button rather than adjusting 50 individual dimmers.

questions.q: In the PEC, what is the 'Color Code' for a Neutral wire in a multi-conductor cable?
questions.n: White is the universal standard for neutral wires to ensure they are never mistaken for energized hot wires.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an 'Emergency Lighting' system that uses its own internal battery pack?
o: To make the exit signs look more modern
To provide illumination for safe egress when the main power fails
To save energy during the day
questions.n: These lights must turn on instantly when they sense a loss of utility voltage so people can find the exits.

questions.q: Which term describes the total power 'available' in an AC circuit, calculated by multiplying Volts and Amps (VA)?
questions.n: Apparent power is the total VA, while 'True Power' (Watts) is what actually does the work after accounting for the power factor.

questions.q: Why is it important to use 'Twist-on Wire Connectors' (Wire Nuts) instead of just electrical tape for joining wires?
o: Because they are cheaper than tape
To prevent the wires from getting wet
To provide a secure mechanical connection and insulation in one step
To make the wires easier to see
questions.n: The spring inside the nut tightly binds the copper together, preventing loose connections that cause heat and fires.

questions.q: In a 230V system, how many 'Hot' wires are present in a standard single-phase residential connection in the Philippines?
questions.n: The Philippine system typically uses two 115V hot wires to provide 230V across them for most household needs.

questions.q: What is the primary reason the PEC requires conduits to be 'reamed' (smoothed) after they are cut?
o: To make the conduit look better for the client
To remove sharp edges that could damage wire insulation during pulling
To allow the electricity to flow faster
To make the conduit weigh less
questions.n: Pulling wires through a sharp-edged pipe can slice the plastic coating, causing a short circuit inside the conduit.

questions.q: Which lighting fixture is designed to hide the actual lamp from view by reflecting light off a secondary surface (like a ceiling cove)?
questions.n: Indirect lighting uses 'bounced' light to create soft, shadowless illumination that is very comfortable for the eyes.

questions.q: What is the function of the 'Electrolyte' in a lead-acid battery used for a generator's starter?
o: To act as a lubricant for the engine
To facilitate the chemical reaction that produces electricity
To keep the battery cool during use
questions.n: The liquid (usually a mix of water and sulfuric acid) allows ions to move between the plates of the battery.

questions.q: In the Philippines, what is the 'Nominal Voltage' for a large commercial customer who has their own transformer on-site?
questions.n: Utilities like Meralco often deliver power at high voltages like 13.8kV or 34.5kV to large buildings, which then step it down themselves.

questions.q: In a 230V, single-phase residential system, if a tester shows voltage between the neutral wire and the ground wire, what is the most likely cause?
o: The use of an 8.0 mm² grounding rod
Open neutral or high resistance in the neutral path
questions.n: A voltage reading between neutral and ground often indicates that the neutral is not effectively returning current to the source, causing it to float.

questions.q: Which specific type of lighting fixture is mandated by the Fire Code for high-occupancy buildings to ensure visibility in smoke-filled environments during an evacuation?
o: Illuminated Exit Signs with battery backup
questions.n: RA 9514 requires path-of-travel identification that remains visible even during primary power failure.

questions.q: When designing a 'Power Room' or Transformer Vault, what is the PEC-mandated requirement for the door to ensure safety and accessibility?
o: It must be sliding to save hallway space
It must be at least 1.5 meters wide to fit any transformer
It must open outwards and be equipped with panic hardware
It must be made of solid narra wood for aesthetics
questions.n: This allows for rapid egress in case of an arc flash or fire within the high-voltage room.

questions.q: In the CSI MasterFormat, which division would an architect look into for 'Integrated Automation' and building management systems?
questions.n: Division 25 specifically covers integrated automation, including sensors and controllers for HVAC and lighting.

questions.q: What is the primary technical reason for 'Twisting' the wires in a data cable (like Cat6) used for building intercoms or internet?
o: To identify which wire is hot and which is neutral
To increase the tensile strength of the copper
To make the cable more flexible for pulling through conduits
questions.n: Twisting pairs ensures that interference affects both wires equally, allowing the system to filter it out.

questions.q: Which term describes the phenomenon where a motor draws significantly more current during the first few seconds of starting compared to its normal running state?
questions.n: Motors require a surge of energy to overcome inertia, which must be considered when sizing breakers.

questions.q: For a 'Wet Location' such as an outdoor swimming pool deck, what is the maximum sensitivity (trip level) required for a GFCI to protect personnel?
questions.n: Class A GFCIs are designed to trip at very low levels to prevent heart fibrillation in humans.

questions.q: When installing electrical conduits underground, what is the PEC-mandated 'Minimum Burial Depth' for a PVC conduit under a residential driveway?
questions.n: This depth provides enough soil cover to protect the conduit from the weight of passenger vehicles.

questions.q: In lighting design, if an architect wants to reduce 'Light Trespass' into a neighbor's property, which metric or rating should they check on the luminaire?
questions.n: The BUG rating quantifies how much light is directed in unwanted directions.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a 'Neutral Bar' in a residential panel board?
o: To trip the main breaker during a short circuit
To provide a common return point for all branch circuit current
To increase the voltage for heavy appliances
To dissipate lightning strikes into the earth
questions.n: The neutral bar collects the 'spent' current from all 230V circuits to return it to the transformer.

questions.q: Which part of a circuit breaker is responsible for the 'Magnetic' trip during a high-current short circuit?
questions.n: A sudden surge of current creates a magnetic field that instantly pulls a lever to trip the breaker.

questions.q: In a '3-way switch' circuit, what are the two wires called that connect the two switches together?
questions.n: Traveler wires provide two alternate paths for current between the switches to allow multi-location control.

questions.q: According to the PEC, what is the maximum percentage of a conduit's cross-sectional area that can be occupied if it contains three or more wires?
questions.n: This limit ensures there is enough air space for heat dissipation and to prevent damage during wire pulling.

questions.q: What is the primary architectural purpose of a 'Cove Lighting' detail?
o: To provide high-intensity task lighting for reading
To highlight a specific piece of artwork on a wall
To satisfy emergency exit lighting requirements
To provide soft, indirect ambient light by reflecting it off the ceiling
questions.n: Cove lights are hidden in a ledge, using the ceiling as a secondary reflector for a glare-free glow.

questions.q: Which electrical unit of measure is equivalent to 'One Joule per Second'?
questions.n: Wattage is the rate of energy transfer, defined as one joule of work per second.

questions.q: In a residential kitchen, why is it standard practice to have at least two 20-amp 'Small Appliance' branch circuits?
o: To ensure the lighting never flickers
To comply with the Fire Code's requirement for oven safety
To provide 3-phase power to the refrigerator
To handle high-wattage items like blenders, toasters, and microwaves simultaneously
questions.n: Kitchen appliances draw significant power; splitting them prevents frequent breaker tripping.

questions.q: Which component of a generator's 'Exhaust System' is specifically designed to reduce the noise produced by the engine?
questions.n: Just like a car, the muffler dampens the sound waves from the combustion process.

questions.q: What is the standard 'Center-to-Center' spacing for wall receptacles in a typical residential room to ensure no point along the floor line is more than 1.8 meters from an outlet?
questions.n: Spacing outlets every 12 feet ensures that a 6-foot cord can reach an outlet from any point along the wall.

questions.q: Which specific professional is required to sign the 'Electrical Permitting' documents for a project with a total connected load exceeding 5 kVA?
questions.n: RA 7920 mandates that only a PEE can sign and seal plans for larger electrical installations.

questions.q: In a lighting plan, what does the symbol of a circle with two parallel lines through it typically represent?
questions.n: This is the universal drafting symbol for a standard wall plug with two receptacles.

questions.q: Which type of 'Circuit Breaker' enclosure is required for a panel board located in a dusty woodshop or textile mill?
questions.n: NEMA 12 enclosures are industrial-grade and designed to exclude dust, lint, and fibers.

questions.q: When a wire is described as 'Stranded' instead of 'Solid', what is the primary benefit for the electrician?
o: It has a higher ampacity for the same gauge
It is much easier to pull through conduits and around bends
questions.n: The flexibility of multiple small strands allows the wire to navigate tight corners without kinking.

questions.q: What is the function of a 'Grounding Rod' (Electrode) driven into the earth outside a building?
o: To filter out 'noise' from the internet connection
To dissipate surge energy from lightning and stabilize voltage relative to the ground
To act as the return path for all standard household current
To prevent the meter from spinning too fast
questions.n: The rod provides a physical connection to the earth's mass to safely discharge high-voltage events.

questions.q: In the Philippines, a 2.0 mm² wire is roughly equivalent to which American Wire Gauge (AWG) size?
questions.n: 14 AWG is the standard size for 15-amp lighting circuits, matching the 2.0 mm² metric equivalent.

questions.q: What is the primary architectural disadvantage of using 'High-Pressure Sodium' (HPS) lamps for indoor office lighting?
o: They are too quiet and don't provide white noise
They last too long, making maintenance schedules difficult
They use too little energy to be effective
Very poor color rendering (CRI), making everything look yellow/orange
questions.n: HPS is efficient but its monochromatic spectrum makes it unsuitable for tasks requiring color accuracy.

questions.q: Which component is needed to transition from an underground PVC conduit to an overhead service drop on a utility pole?
questions.n: The weatherhead allows wires to exit the conduit while preventing rain from entering the top of the pipe.

questions.q: Why does the PEC require a 'Dedicated' circuit for an electric water heater?
o: To prevent the water from becoming electrified
To ensure its high continuous current draw doesn't overload circuits shared with other items
To allow the heater to run on DC power
questions.n: Water heaters draw thousands of watts; sharing the line would trip the breaker immediately.

questions.q: What is the purpose of 'Bus Duct' or 'Busway' in a high-rise building's vertical shaft?
o: To provide a path for the elevator to travel
To efficiently transport large amounts of current to multiple floors without many separate wires
To store backup batteries for the emergency lights
To act as a ventilation shaft for the bathrooms
questions.n: Busways are prefabricated metal troughs with solid copper bars that serve as a high-capacity spine.

questions.q: In a generator, the 'Control Panel' includes a safety feature that automatically shuts down the engine if which condition is detected?
o: The exterior lights are turned on
questions.n: Low oil pressure can cause catastrophic engine failure; the system shuts down to protect the hardware.

questions.q: Which lighting term describes the 'sparkle' or 'glint' produced by a small, high-intensity light source?
questions.n: Brilliance is the visual effect of high-intensity points of light that add visual interest to a space.

questions.q: According to the PEC, what is the maximum number of 'Quarter Bends' (90-degree turns) allowed in a single run of conduit between pull points?
o: Unlimited, as long as a lubricant is used
questions.n: Limiting bends ensures that the friction doesn't become so high that the wire insulation is stripped during pulling.

questions.q: Which material is used inside 'Firestop' caulk that causes it to expand when exposed to heat, sealing off conduit penetrations?
questions.n: Intumescent substances swell significantly when heated, creating a char layer that blocks fire and smoke.

questions.q: What is the standard 'Unit of Measurement' for Illuminance (the amount of light hitting a surface) in the metric system?
questions.n: One Lux is defined as one lumen per square meter.

questions.q: In a large commercial facility, a 'Power Factor Correction' capacitor bank is used to reduce which of the following?
o: The number of circuit breakers needed
questions.n: Capacitors offset the inductive load from motors, reducing the wasted 'reactive' power the utility must supply.

questions.q: Why is it dangerous to use a 'Standard' light switch to control a large industrial motor directly?
o: The switch is too small for the user's hand to operate
The motor's high inductive load can create a damaging arc that melts the switch contacts
The switch will make the motor spin in the wrong direction
The switch will increase the motor's speed beyond its limit
questions.n: Motors require 'motor-rated' switches or contactors designed to handle the intense sparking of high-current startup.

questions.q: What is the primary technical difference between a 'Step-Down' transformer and a 'Step-Up' transformer?
o: One uses copper and the other uses gold
The color of the outer casing
The ratio of turns between the primary and secondary coils
Step-down transformers only work at night
questions.n: A higher number of turns on the output side increases voltage, while fewer turns decrease it.

questions.q: In the Philippines, which color is used to identify the 'Grounding' conductor in a flexible power cord for a laptop or appliance?
o: Green or Green with Yellow stripes
questions.n: This is the international and PEC-recognized color for the safety ground wire.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a 'Pull Box' in a long run of electrical conduit?
o: To protect the wires from lightning
To house the main circuit breaker
To step down the voltage for the next floor
To provide an intermediate point to make pulling long wires easier and safer
questions.n: Breaking a long run into segments prevents excessive tension on the wires and the conduit itself.

questions.q: Which specific lighting fixture is best for providing 'Task Lighting' in a commercial kitchen over a food prep table?
o: Under-cabinet LED strips or high-CRI recessed spots
questions.n: Focused light on the work surface ensures safety and accuracy for food preparation.

questions.q: In a 'Transfer Switch', what is the purpose of the 'Interlock' mechanism?
o: To prevent the generator and utility power from being connected at the same time
To lock the generator in place so it can't be stolen
To ensure the generator starts exactly at 6:00 PM
To increase the voltage during a power surge
questions.n: Feeding generator power back into utility lines (backfeeding) is deadly for utility workers and can destroy the generator.

questions.q: What is the primary technical reason for using 'Silver' or 'Gold' plating on high-end audio or data connectors?
o: Because they are better insulators than plastic
To make the cables look more expensive to the client
To prevent oxidation and maintain a low-resistance connection over time
To allow the cable to carry 230V power safely
questions.n: Gold doesn't corrode, ensuring the signal remains clear even in humid environments like the Philippines.

questions.q: According to the PEC, what is the 'Minimum Working Space' height required in front of electrical equipment?
questions.n: This ensures that a technician of average height can stand comfortably and move safely while working on the panel.

questions.q: In lighting design, what is 'Luminous Efficacy'?
o: The ratio of light produced (lumens) to the power consumed (watts)
The angle at which light leaves the fixture
The amount of heat generated by the fixture
The time it takes for a bulb to reach full brightness
questions.n: Efficacy tells you how efficient a bulb is at converting electricity into visible light.

questions.q: Which type of 'Battery' is most commonly used for the 'Starting System' of a large diesel generator in a commercial building?
questions.n: Lead-acid batteries are reliable and provide the high 'cranking amps' needed to start a large engine.

questions.q: What does a 'Photo-sensor' (or Photocontrol) do when installed on an outdoor parking lot light?
o: It takes pictures of cars for security purposes
It turns the light on at dusk and off at dawn based on ambient light levels
It increases the brightness if it sees a person
It detects movement to turn the lights on
questions.n: Photosensors automate lighting based on sunlight, saving energy by ensuring lights only run when dark.

questions.q: Why is it important to have a 'Main Disconnect' switch located outside a building near the utility meter?
o: To protect the house from solar flares
To allow neighbors to turn off your lights if they are too bright
To allow firefighters to quickly cut all power before entering a burning building
To make it easier for the utility company to disconnect you for non-payment
questions.n: An exterior disconnect ensures safety for first responders by eliminating electrocution risks during firefighting.

questions.q: In a '3-phase' system, what is the angular difference between each of the three voltage phases?
questions.n: This offset ensures that power delivery is constant and smooth, as one phase is always at or near its peak.

questions.q: What is the function of a 'Choke' or 'Inductor' in an older lighting ballast?
o: To prevent the fixture from getting dusty
To change the color of the light to cool white
To act as a backup battery
To limit the flow of current after the lamp has started
questions.n: Once a gas-discharge lamp starts, its resistance drops; the choke prevents the lamp from drawing too much current and exploding.

questions.q: Which specific professional is authorized by the Philippine Electrical Code to perform electrical installations in a small residence?
questions.n: RMEs are licensed to install, operate, and maintain electrical systems up to 500 kVA and 600 volts.

questions.q: What is the primary risk of using 'Undersized' wires for a long-distance run to an outdoor gate motor?
o: The wire will turn into a magnet and attract metal debris
The motor will consume less electricity and save money
The motor will spin too fast and break the gate
Excessive voltage drop, causing the motor to run hot or fail to start
questions.n: Small wires have higher resistance; over long distances, too much voltage is lost as heat before reaching the motor.
